Area.evidence_source: In the UK, the Social Exclusion Unit (Office of the Deputy Prime Minister, 2005) has drawn attention to the transitional experience of young adulthood and the risks this entails for young people experiencing high levels of deprivation in combination with other needs. However, this study of student suicide suggests that the risks associated with transition can be high even for more affluent groups of young people in the relatively sheltered setting of HE. Within this broad context of transition, the sense of being 'inbetween' may be heightened at the start and finish of the academic year. The experience of transition may weaken support networks whilst exposing students with existing vulnerabilities to heightened fears about the future. The participants in this study characterised the response to this experience of transition as a state of entrapment from which suicide was conceptualised as a release.
